decision: Implement a pure-Go, stdio JSON-RPC LSP client and the read-only lsp tool first; no cgo and no bundled language servers.

package_layout.rule: The core package owns config/discovery, JSON-RPC transport, client lifecycle, documents, positions, diagnostics and edits. It must not import internal/server, internal/cli or internal/tools/builtin. The tool schema, approval metadata and registration live in the adapter package.
package_layout.maintenance: Maintain lsp as an independent Go package: its own API, doc.go, fake-server tests and package gates. It must be usable without a session, HTTP server or tool registry.

goal_beyond_request: Give go_hive agents IDE-level semantic navigation, diagnostics and auditable refactoring, while keeping the release binary pure Go and the language-server ecosystem an explicit external dependency.

problem.statement: go_hive has no semantic code-intelligence surface. Text search and AST search can locate syntax, but cannot answer what a symbol means, where it is defined, which files reference it, or whether a rename is type-safe.
user_value: Ask the same language server an editor uses for definitions, references, types, diagnostics and fixes.
Perform semantic renames that follow imports, re-exports and cross-file references.
Use it only when a matching project marker and server binary exist; never invent a result when no server is available.
Keep the Go core CGO_ENABLED=0; language servers remain external processes selected by the user.
problem.why_not_now: This is a post-1.0 opt-in capability. Hive upstream has no lsp tool or LSP client, so this is not part of the current parity claim.

requirements.statement: Expose a model-facing tool named lsp whose action enum covers the read-only set first: status, capabilities, diagnostics, definition, type_definition, implementation, references, hover and symbols.
requirements.acceptance: Tool definition and action validation are frozen by a golden test; unknown actions fail closed.

requirements.statement: Implement the client with Go stdlib only: JSON-RPC over stdio, Content-Length framing, request IDs, cancellation, timeouts and process lifecycle.
requirements.acceptance: A fake LSP server exercises initialize, request, notification, response, error, cancel, crash and restart; no new Go module is required.

requirements.statement: Auto-detect servers from embedded defaults and user config ($HIVE_HOME/lsp.json): cwd-only root markers by default, an optional absolute per-server rootDir pin, fileTypes, disabled, local-bin then PATH command resolution.
requirements.acceptance: Config precedence, shallow merge, object-field replacement, disabled, unresolved-binary and rootDir parse/validate/rooted cases pass table tests.

requirements.statement: Map LSP UTF-16 positions to Go byte offsets and back for line/symbol resolution, including CRLF, CJK and emoji.
requirements.acceptance: Round-trip matrix covers ASCII, CJK, emoji, tabs, CRLF and a symbol repeated on the same line with #N.

requirements.statement: Synchronize only the documents a request needs: didOpen, full-text didChange, didClose after idle, version tracking and disk reconciliation.
requirements.acceptance: Document manager tests cover open, change, stale version, external edit, closed file, symlink and non-regular file refusal.

requirements.statement: Return a bounded, deterministic result: grouped locations with file:line:col context, diagnostics severity sorting, dedupe, caps and no-match text.
requirements.acceptance: Golden output tests cover definition/references/hover/symbols/diagnostics, truncation and server failure text.

requirements.statement: Apply semantic write actions only with explicit approval: rename as a preview by default, then apply; code_actions; rename_file.
requirements.acceptance: Preview and apply goldens, WorkspaceEdit validation, conflicting edits, version mismatch and rollback tests pass.

requirements.statement: Bound every request and workspace scan: tool timeout 5..300s, startup, project-load, diagnostics, process count, glob and symbol caps.
requirements.acceptance: Timeout, cancellation, idle shutdown, crash backoff, max-process and oversized-frame tests pass.

requirements.statement: Do not expose arbitrary LSP requests to the model in v1. request is deferred until the read and write surfaces are audited.
requirements.acceptance: Schema rejects request; no raw method dispatch path is reachable from the tool.

requirements.statement: Keep server configuration and execution trustworthy: model cannot choose binary/args; config comes only from $HIVE_HOME/lsp.json; secrets and server stderr stay out of normal tool output.
requirements.acceptance: Config-to-command path; malicious config; stderr redaction; workspace-root and symlink tests pass.

non_goals: Do not bundle gopls, pyright, rust-analyzer or any language server in the go_hive release archive.
Do not add a DAP/debugger client in this feature; that is a separate protocol and product surface.
Do not implement a full VS Code-compatible client in v1; only the capabilities the tool actions need.
Do not claim parity with omp's 55-server catalog; ship an embedded catalog and test a representative subset, with custom servers supported through config.
Do not support YAML config in v1 unless a YAML dependency is separately approved. JSON is the v1 format.
Do not expose raw LSP request, remote LSP, browser/editor UI, or background workspace indexing in v1.
assumptions: A user who wants LSP can install a language server; absence is an explicit unavailable result, not a reason to fake semantics.

The session directory is the default workspace root; root-marker detection follows the omp cwd-only rule, not a parent-directory walk. Configuration is separate: it comes only from $HIVE_HOME/lsp.json (there is no session-level file). A definition may instead pin an absolute rootDir, which becomes that server's workspace root.
Read-only actions are safe to auto-run within the tool policy; rename, code actions and file renames require explicit write approval.
All source positions are converted through one position mapper; no tool path is allowed to use raw byte columns as LSP columns.

options.name: Use a Go LSP library
options.reason: The protocol surface needed here is small and stateful; an external library adds dependency and lifecycle semantics we would still have to audit. Stdlib keeps CGO=0 and the release surface controlled.

options.name: Embed tree-sitter / ast-grep instead
options.reason: Syntax parsing cannot answer type, reference or rename semantics. It is a different feature; ast_grep remains the syntactic fallback.

options.name: Pure-Go stdio JSON-RPC client + external servers
options.reason: No cgo, no new Go dependency, matches the LSP ecosystem and keeps server installation explicit. The work is in lifecycle, document sync and edit safety.

options.name: Shared broker / lspmux in v1
options.reason: Useful for multi-session reuse, but adds a daemon, socket protocol and cross-session document cleanup. Private per-project clients first.

D1.title: Tool surface
D1.text: Register lsp only when $HIVE_HOME/lsp.json settings.enabled is true. V1 registers the read-only actions and returns a typed unsupported-action error for write actions until P1. The full target enum is documented but not exposed as a false promise.

D2.title: Transport and lifecycle
D2.text: One process per (workspace, server) with a reader goroutine and a writer protected by a mutex. Frame with Content-Length; cap frame size; route responses by JSON-RPC id; turn notifications into events; cancel with $/cancelRequest; kill the process group on shutdown. Initialize with processId, clientInfo, rootUri, workspaceFolders and only the capabilities the client implements.

D3.title: Config and discovery
D3.text: The independent internal/lsp loader merges embedded defaults with $HIVE_HOME/lsp.json only. The session directory is the file tools' sandbox root and is agent-writable, so <sessionDir>/.hive/lsp.json and .hive/lsp.local.json are never read (see go_hive/docs/config-roots.html). Shallow merge per server; object-valued fields replace as a whole. Auto-detect requires a workspace root marker and a resolvable command in workspace-local bins first, then PATH; a definition may pin an absolute validated rootDir instead, which roots discovery, local bins, the server process cwd/rootUri, documents and workspace scans there. Invalid new servers are ignored with a warning; invalid overrides retain the previous definition, and a missing rootDir directory reports the server as unrooted with a reason.

D4.title: Action router
D4.text: Resolve file -> server by fileTypes, excluding disabled servers and preferring primary over isLinter. Read-only actions use one client lookup. Workspace forms are explicit: diagnostics/symbols can use file='*'; status ignores file; capabilities may inspect all. No request action in v1.

D5.title: Position mapper
D5.text: LSP positions are zero-based line plus UTF-16 code units. Build a per-line index from UTF-8 bytes to UTF-16 columns and back. Resolve symbol columns with identifier boundaries, exact case first then case-insensitive, occurrence selector name#N, line-local only. Never use Go byte offsets as LSP character offsets.

D6.title: Document manager
D6.text: Track uri, languageId, version, text and last-used time. Open a document before a position request; reconcile from disk when the file changed; send didChange with the full text for v1; close idle documents after five minutes. Refuse non-regular files and paths outside the workspace.

D7.title: Diagnostics and results
D7.text: Keep push diagnostics per URI/version. For a single file wait for a fresh publish or pull diagnostic if supported; do not call an empty stale publish clean. Sort by severity and range; dedupe by range+message. Render deterministic text; cap references and symbols; expose structured details for the UI.

D8.title: Workspace edits
D8.text: Parse both changes and documentChanges. Validate URIs, versions, ranges and overlapping edits before touching disk. Apply per-file with a temp file and atomic rename; keep enough original bytes to roll back the whole operation on failure. rename defaults to preview, apply requires explicit approval; rename_file sends willRenameFiles/didRenameFiles and rolls back reference edits if the filesystem move fails.

D9.title: Timeouts and resource bounds
D9.text: Tool timeout 5..300s, default 20s. Warmup 5s; project-load wait 15s; single-file diagnostics 3s; glob diagnostics 400ms/file; max 20 glob files; max 200 workspace symbols; max 50 contextual references; max 2 workspace checkers. Idle client sweep 60s; open document idle 5min; failed initialization backoff 3min.

D10.title: Security and trust
D10.text: Server command and args come only from embedded defaults or $HIVE_HOME/lsp.json, never from model input. Do not log secrets or full environment. Redact stderr to a bounded tail. Enforce workspace-root and symlink checks. Write actions are approval-gated. Raw request is absent in v1.

config_contract.authority: LSP configuration is owned by the independent internal/lsp package. One operator-level JSON config file ($HIVE_HOME/lsp.json) is merged over embedded defaults; configuration.json and session-directory files are not LSP config sources in v1.
config_contract.format: JSON only in v1. YAML is deliberately out of scope until a YAML dependency is separately approved.

files.note: 55 server definitions shipped as data, not a promise that every server is installed.
The only on-disk level. Session-directory files are agent-writable and are never read (see go_hive/docs/config-roots.html).

config_contract.merge: The user file is merged over the built-in defaults. Per-server merge is shallow: a user server object overrides top-level fields; settings, initOptions, capabilities and workspaceReadyTimings replace as whole objects, never deep-merge. Servers absent from the user file retain built-in values.
config_contract.cache: Load and cache the merged config per home. Root-marker and binary discovery are evaluated against the workspace root (session directory) unless a server definition pins rootDir, in which case they use that absolute directory; no parent-directory walk either way.
config_contract.reload: After changing $HIVE_HOME/lsp.json, root markers or installed binaries, call lsp action=reload file=*; reload clears the home cache and restarts servers whose identity changed.

catalog.rule: Catalog entries are data, not a promise that every server is installed or certified. The acceptance suite tests a representative cross-language subset and records missing binaries as an external evidence gap.

acceptance.pass: lsp name, action enum, required fields and approval metadata match the frozen contract.
unknown action, missing file/query/new_name, invalid payload and request action all fail closed.
initialize, initialized, request, response, notification, error, cancel, crash and restart pass.
split frames, extra headers, oversized frame, malformed JSON and EOF are handled without panic.
precedence, shallow merge, object replacement, disabled, missing binary, cwd-only root marker, optional rootDir parse/validate/rooted and custom server pass.
ASCII, CJK, emoji, tabs, CRLF and #N round-trip exactly.
open, full change, external edit, stale version, idle close, non-regular and symlink cases pass.
definition/references/hover/symbols/diagnostics text, sorting, dedupe, caps and no-match text match goldens.
preview, apply, overlap, version mismatch, rollback and rename_file pass with no partial mutation.
timeouts, $/cancelRequest, process crash backoff, idle close and max-process cap pass.
config command injection, path escape, symlink escape, stderr redaction and write approval checks pass.
CGO_ENABLED=0 go test and six GOOS/GOARCH builds pass.
with gopls installed, definition/references/hover/diagnostics/rename run against a fixture module; if absent, recorded as an external gap, not a pass.
no new Go module; no bundled server; runtime missing-server text is explicit.

queued or ignored by version, never reported as current

risks.risk: LSP servers are heavy and may take seconds to initialize
risks.impact: first call latency and user-visible timeouts
risks.mitigation: lazy start, bounded project-load wait, idle shutdown, explicit status and no silent fallback.

risks.risk: UTF-16 position conversion is easy to get subtly wrong
risks.impact: queries hit wrong columns or corrupt edits
risks.mitigation: single position mapper, CJK/emoji/CRLF matrix, never use byte columns directly.

risks.risk: WorkspaceEdit application can partially mutate a project
risks.mitigation: validate all edits first, atomic per-file writes, transaction rollback, preview default for rename.

risks.risk: Config execution is a trust boundary
risks.mitigation: embedded/user config only, model cannot set command/args, write approval, path and stderr controls.

risks.risk: 55-server catalog is broader than the tested set
risks.mitigation: call the catalog data; test seven representative servers; missing binaries are evidence gaps, not passes.

risks.risk: No shared broker means duplicate servers across sessions
risks.mitigation: defer shared mux; cap processes; start private clients only.

open_questions: Should v1 read-only ship before write actions, or is rename required in the first release?
Which representative servers are mandatory for acceptance: gopls + pyright, or all seven?
